title: Flask publish on different local ip than the machine it deployed on inside a docker
q_body: I am using docker with a flask app inside to display the visual results in a browser. I have created the image with the flask inside, tested on my machine (an Ubuntu 24.04 machine) and it seems to work fine. Flask reports 2 ips (the localhost and the actual ip of my pc) which can be accessible from my machine (through a browser) or even from other machines (the port has been open in my machine). The problem I am facing is that when I try to deploy it on a server the same docker does not seem to work as expected. Let me summarise the issues I encounter: a) The reported ips are: * Running on all addresses (0.0.0.0) * Running on http://127.0.0.1:5000 * Running on http://172.17.0.2:5000 the first one is the localhost so it should be available from the same machine (if I am not mistaken) while the second one should be also accessible from a local network, right? I have exposed the port 5000 from within the docker (in both machines). Should I include the parameter: -p 5000:5000 when I run my docker for example? b) The reported second ip is a private ip also if I am not mistaken. I was expected a public ip to be exposed. In my first pc we have static ips, maybe this is the reason for not being able to see a public ip? c) If we suppose a public ip is not available, then a local one is provided. But it seems peculiar that it is not the server's ip. I am using another ip (another local one) to connect to the server via ssh: ssh username@172.22.10.10 How is it possible for flask to expose a different local ip than the actual ip of the machine it is deployed on (even on a docker)?

title: The result obtained from the OpenCV-Python cv.add() function differs from the official documentation
q_body: During my learning process of OpenCV-Python, I encountered an issue. My environment uses Python version 3.13, NumPy version 2.2.6, and OpenCV-Python version 4.12. In the "Arithmetic Operations on Images" section of the official documentation, it mentions the difference between OpenCV addition and NumPy addition: OpenCV addition is a saturated operation while NumPy addition is a modulo operation. Official documentation page However, the actual results I obtained during computation differ from the values provided in the documentation. My code: import cv2 as cv import numpy as np x = np.uint8([250]) y = np.uint8([10]) print(f"x+y = {x+y}") print(f"cv.add(x,y) = {cv.add(x,y)}") Official documentation result: [4] [[255]] My result: [4] [[260.] [0.] [0.] [0.]] I checked cv.add(x,y).dtype and found it returns float64 instead of uint8 . After attempting data type conversion and retrieving the first value with cv.add(x,y).astype(np.uint8)[0] , the result is [4], which matches the NumPy addition result. How can I obtain the correct value from the cv.add() algorithm?

title: How to inject a global httpx.AsyncClient session in FastAPI using dependency injection?
q_body: I'm using FastAPI and want to share an httpx.AsyncClient session across requests using dependency injection. I followed a pattern using FastAPI's lifespan function and storing the session in app.state as follows: # Standard library imports from contextlib import asynccontextmanager from typing import AsyncGenerator, cast, Dict # Third party library imports import httpx from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, Depends @asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncGenerator[None, None]: async with httpx.AsyncClient() as session: app.state.session = session yield async def get_session(request: Request) -> httpx.AsyncClient: return cast(httpx.AsyncClient, request.app.state.session) app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan) @app.get("/") async def root(session: httpx.AsyncClient = Depends(get_session)) -> Dict[str, int]: response = await session.get("https://www.stackoverflow.com") return {"status": response.status_code} if __name__ == "__main__": import uvicorn uvicorn.run(app) This works well, but I’m wondering: are there alternative approaches to injecting a shared httpx.AsyncClient session in FastAPI? What are the potential drawbacks of this pattern?
